name: The Beverly Hills Hotel
address: 9641 Sunset Boulevard, Beverly Hills, CA 90210, United States
tagline: The Pink Palace on Sunset: 209 rooms, suites and bungalows in 12 acres of garden.
description:
The Beverly Hills Hotel is a Dorchester Collection hotel at 9641 Sunset Boulevard, known as the Pink Palace. It has 209 rooms and suites, many of them bungalows hidden in 12 acres of tropical garden, and a pool that has been in use since 1938.

The hotel opened on 12 May 1912, before the city of Beverly Hills existed, and its founder was Margaret Anderson. It was first painted pink in 1948. The architect Paul R. Williams built the Crescent Wing in 1949 and reworked the lobby, the Polo Lounge and the Fountain Coffee Room. The banana-leaf Martinique wallpaper, created in 1942, is the hotel's signature wall covering.

Rooms begin with the 37 square metre Superior Room, and the Bungalow Room, at 44 square metres, sits among the gardens. The Paul R. Williams Suite covers 135 square metres with a grand piano, a bar and a large patio. Bungalow 5 has 122 square metres with a private pool and jacuzzi, and can connect to make a four-bedroom suite. The Presidential Bungalow has 170 square metres, a private infinity plunge pool on its patio, a chef's kitchen and a dining room for ten. Many suites include complimentary round-trip airport transfers.

The Polo Lounge, with its candy-striped ceiling, serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and a Sunday brunch; its McCarthy Salad was first served here. The Fountain Coffee Room, a 1950s-style counter diner, has served guests since 1949. The Cabana Cafe serves light meals beside the pool.

The pool opened in 1938 as the Sand and Pool Club. It has poolside cabanas for four guests, and the pool is for hotel guests only, open daily from 7 am to 10 pm. The hotel spa has treatment rooms, a duet suite and steam showers, and a gym is open to guests around the clock. A house car takes guests anywhere within three miles. Rodeo Drive is a five-minute drive, and Los Angeles International Airport is about 30 to 40 minutes away.

The hotel suits travellers who want Old Hollywood's best-known address and a private bungalow in a garden. Up to two house-trained dogs are welcome.
